question.prompt:
A rectangle, with sides parallel to the \(x\)-axis and \(y\)-axis, has opposite vertices located at \((15, 3)\) and \((16, 5).\) A line is drawn through points \(A(0, 0)\) and \(B(3, 1).\) Another line is drawn through points \(C(0, 10)\) and \(D(2, 9).\) How many points on the rectangle lie on at least one of the two lines?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q07_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The rectangle occupies horizontal positions from \(x=15\) to \(x=16\), and vertical positions from \(y=3\) to \(y=5\). We only need to see where each line lies over that narrow horizontal interval.

From \(A(0,0)\) to \(B(3,1)\), the first line rises \(1\) unit for every \(3\) units to the right, so its equation is \(y=x/3\). At \(x=15\), it reaches \(y=5\), the rectangle's upper-left corner. For every \(x>15\), it is above \(y=5\), so it touches the rectangle only at \((15,5)\).

From \(C(0,10)\) to \(D(2,9)\), the second line falls \(1\) unit for every \(2\) units to the right, giving \(y=10-x/2\). At \(x=15\), its height is \(2.5\), already below the rectangle. It falls farther as \(x\) increases, so it never reaches the rectangle.

The completed official plot shows the corner contact and the other line below the rectangle.

[Figure 2](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q07_solution_official_completed_plot.png)

There is exactly \(\boxed{1}\) point on at least one of the lines, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). Checking a line over the rectangle's actual range of \(x\)-values avoids having to extend the entire drawing.
solutions.title: Compare each line height with the rectangle over 15 <= x <= 16
